qs.q: An immunocompromised transplant patient develops progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy. Brain biopsy reveals demyelination and abnormal glial cells. Which viral family is the causative agent classified under?
o: Poxviridae family consisting of large, complex double-stranded DNA brick-shaped viruses.
Paramyxoviruses family comprising enveloped single-stranded negative-sense RNA agents.
Polyomaviridae family including small, non-enveloped double-stranded circular DNA viruses.
Picornaviridae family containing small non-enveloped positive-sense RNA human pathogens.
Caliciviridae family including small round non-enveloped viruses causing gastroenteritis.
qs.e: JC virus, the cause of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, belongs to the Polyomaviridae family.

qs.q: Which pathological finding is observed within oligodendroglial nuclei in Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)?
qs.e: Oligodendroglial nuclear viral inclusions are characteristic of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy. Alpha-synuclein glial cytoplasmic inclusions are instead found in Multiple System Atrophy.
